speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
Well, it is increasing all the time. It is just that class of service that increases with increasing business ; $10,000 was the appropriation voted last year.
iMr. TAYLOR. It has overrun that by about 50 per cent. That is a very poor estimate, knowing what each instrument costs and knowing how many you require.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: There is an explanation of it which we have to give regarding one or two other items, and it is a reason that is not entirely satisfactory to myself. It is that there has grown up in the department the practice of allowing some of the accounts of one year to run over into another year, with the result that they have had to take from this year's appropriation to meet the balance due from the previous year. I think the system is a bad one ; I think it should be changed as far as possible, and I am glad to see the hon. minister is asking for a sufficient amount to close up the accounts for the chrrent year. In that case $10,000 would be enough to pay the accounts for the current year, but if the accounts are passed over into the next year there is a difficulty in making the calculations.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: In 1S96-97, when the government brought down their estimates, they found fault with the previous government for having pursued that practice, and in nearly every case they asked for money enough to wipe off old debts.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: That is the right way.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: They did that, and it was never going to happen again ; but now with nearly every item that comes up the money is required to pay overlapping accounts. '

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I quite agree with my hon. friend that it is the better way to take a sufficient sum to close up the accounts for the current year rather than that they should be carried over. I would rather, as Minister of Finance, give a sufficient sum to close up the accounts for the year than have these accounts hanging over. That is what we are proposing to do in this case.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
This is a similar case. There was as much as $28,000 paid out of this year's appropriation for accounts that bad accumulated. The vote proposed is intended to cover all the accounts for the current year, and we are asking for the coming year $140,000.
Mr. OSLE'R. Have you the amount expended on rented buildings ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
We are coming to an item in a few moments when I will give that information to the hon. gentleman.
Ottawa public buildings-heating, including salaries of engineers, firemen and watchmen, $18,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The appropriation in the main estimates was $87,000. With the additional amount we now propose it will -make it $105,000. The chief item in this is for coal supplied by the contractors, Messrs. John Heney & Son, Ottawa. We paid last year $6.90 per ton. The general amount consumed for some years was 6,000 tons, but last year it was necessary to order an additional 1,000 tons.
What kind of coal ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Anthracite.
That does not include all the coal ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This is for the Ottawa buildings.
Is the coal that was burnt in this building included ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: All the furnace coal is hard coal, but for grate purposes some soft coal is used.
What is the rate at which that is purchased ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
For the grates they use Cannel coal, which is purchased at $8.45 per ton.
Ottawa public buildings-elevator attendants, $1,900.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
This is asked to supplement a vote of $10,000 which was made by parliament last year to cover the cost of running the elevators in the public buildings, the parliament building, the east and west departmental buildings, the Langevin block and the Woods' building.
Ottawa public buildings-gas and electric light, $4,'250.
Ottawa public buildings-including repairs, ventilation and lighting, furniture, &c., $40,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: There was an appropriation in the main estimates of $125,000. We are asking for $40,000, which will make it $165,000.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Why are you asking for this large sum ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
iMr. FIELDING. We had an appropriation in the main estimates of $24,000. This is another case of arrears. The appropriation will probably be sufficient for the year's service, but there were considerable arrears, and it is proposed to take a sufficient vote to cover them. The appropriation proposed for the coming year is $24,000. We are not increasing the amount. We are asking for

a sufficient appropriation to pay these arrears.
Ottawa public building3-grounds, $1,250.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Is this on account of the heavy snow ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This $1,250 is to be obtained for the purpose of covering arrears accumulated during the past few years in keeping the grounds on Parliament Hill and the Lovers' Walk in proper condition. I think in consideration of the Lovers' Walk, it should be passed without objection.

I notice that the hon. acting Minister of Public Works says that this is to cover arrears. I think when he tells us about these arrears, he should be able to tell us the amount of the arrears overlapping in each of these cases.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: It is really the amount we are asking-about $1,250. Actually it is $1,249.70. Of course, that would be paid in the early part of the season out of the general vote, and in the latter part of the season they would be short just that amount to pay current expenses.
That is not the way I understand the hon. minister is putting it.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Then in that ease I am afraid I have been misleading my hon. friend. At the beginning of the year, out of the appropriation the balance of last year's account will be paid, and at the end of the year we will be short just that amount.
I want to know what these amounts were for V

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
$747 will be applied to the payment of gardeners' and labourers' wages. $445.74 is for plants, 'manure, &c., and $56.98 for sundries. Total, $1,249.70.
Ottawa public buildings-Major's Hill park, $1,500.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
The details are as follows :	Manure and earth, $283.98 ; plants,
$171.41 ; sundries, $63'65; gardener's wages, &c., $871.7S.
Dominion public buildings-furniture, $5,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The number of these buildings is increasing and consequently this item increases.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: The government are lavish in buying furniture both for Dominion buildings and Ottawa buildings.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I do not think that any of the furniture in these apartments is too luxurious for the parliament of Canada or in any way extravagant.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: I notice a large quantity of steel shelves going to the different departments.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
There is a special vote for that. It is not covered by this vote.
Dominion public buildings-rents, $10,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This to provide the balance required to pay all rents up to the close of the current fiscal year.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Surely the government knew, when they brought in the main estimates, the rent they would have to pay and should not ask an additional $10,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This is on account of buildings acquired during the year in all parts of the country. At iSt. John, New Brunswick, the immigrant building was rented at $950. It was rented from the city council. In the Carry building oil Rideau street, two floors and a basement, were rented for the purposes of the Georgian Bay Canal survey. The rent is for nine months at the rate of $5,285 per annum. The term of rental is two years or a little less, so that it shall end the 1st May.
How many clerks are employed in the offices ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: My deputy thinks 20 to 25.

In Toronto you could rent office accommodation for 150 to 200 clerks for that rental. This is simply an outrage. If this building is rented for that purpose alone, you cannot spend that money without having some sort of a job.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I do not think my hon. friend should rush to that assumption.
In Toronto or Montreal, to pay $5,000 for the purposes of an office connected with the survey would be simply an outrage.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: I draw attention to the fact that this vote is for Dominion public buildings, and you are including in it an Ottawa public building for the Public Works department. The government are paying at the rate of about 25 per cent in money for rentals. Surely the government would do better to borrow at 3 or 4 per cent and put up the buildings we require and not rent from party friends at exorbitant rates. We are paying nearly $3,000 a year for improvements on a building down on Sparks street that was rented for the taking of the census and which it was supposed, would not be required after that work was done. It was continued on at $6,000 a year and the government spent $15,000 or $20,000 in putting in an elevator and refitting the whole place. Why should the government pay theSe exorbitant rentals ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
In coming to a conclusion as to the fairness of the rental one must take each individual case and investigate it. I quite agree that these rented buildings are not the most convenient and for my part I think we should accept the responsibility

6S20
of putting up a new departmental building and concentrating our offices tliere. But these things cannot be done in a day and for the present we have not been able to do it. 1 know that the Minister of Public Works has been giving his attention to this matter, but how far he has succeeded I am not prepared to say. I have not sufficient knowledge of the character of the building to contradict my bon. friend (Mr. Osier) but 1 cannot imagine that the department would pay a grossly extravagant price. I am afraid that nearly every one*thinks the government ought to pay more than a private individual pay a grossly extravagant price. I am afraid it applies to nearly all transactions unless we look very closely after them. If there is any reason to believe that there is anything wrong about the renting of this building I would be glad to have the matter inquired into.

This matter has been before the House for a good many sessions and each year the excuse is put forward that the matter is being looked into, and yet as the Minister of Finance says, they continue to pay extravagant rents.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I did not say that.

I quite agree with the Minister of Finance that the government has to pay more than a private individual has to pay, and I entirely agree with his suggestion that the government should without any delay erect proper buildings of their own. If for the accommodation of twenty or twenty-five clerks engaged in the survey of that canal we are paying over $5,000 for that floor space, it is almost a criminal act to pay it. It is an outrageous price.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Where is this building ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: It is the tall building immediately across the canal on the right-hand side. I have just been told that the Hydrographic Survey of the Marine Department and the Ottawa River Works have offices in this building also. However, that would not enter into the consideration whether or not the rent is fair, and in view of what the hon. gentleman (Mr. Osier) has said we ought to make some inquiry into it.

My criticism was based on the first statement that it was for the accommodation of the survey staff of the canal which would require twenty-five clerks. If there are more clerks it might be that the rent is reasonable.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I have just been told that there are other branches includqd. The question is as to whether that is a fair rent to pay for that amount of floor space, and in that light the number of clerks would not affect the question.
If you rent two floors for twenty or twenty-five clerks you may have twice the room you require.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: That would concern the amount of space but not the rent.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: How much are we paying for the rent of buildings in Ottawa altogether ? I cannot understand why this government will go to a party friend and tell him they will enter into a lease for a number of years if he will erect a building for them. I understand that was done in the case of the Militia building. Surely the government can get money cheaper than a private individual and erect its own buildings. In the same way, for the accommodation of the Surveyor General the government went to a political friend and asked him to put up a building promising to take a lease for so many years and paying an exorbitant rent equal to about 20 per cent on the capital invested. In 1896 the public officials were housed in buildings owned by the government, but every year you are paying higher rentals to accommodate a larger staff and doing very little more work. What rents were paid in 1896 and what rents are paid in Ottawa to-day ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I have not the figures for 1896. The total rents paid in Ottawa now amount to $47,111. I myself favour the idea of the government owning its buildings, but while it might be an unfortunate tiling to rent buildings all over the city it would he more unfortunate for the government to own buildings all over the city. I think we should select a suitable place, possibly one or two suitable places, and put up sufficient buildings to accommodate our officials. The moment the government try to buy land anywhere they immediately find it is very expensive, and the probability is that nothing is lost by delay, because if we push a transaction of that kind we may have to pay an extravagant price. It is one thing to pay an extravagant rent, if it is extravagant, for a year or two and it is another thing to pay an extravagant price for land. The Minister of Public Works is giving the subject his attention with every desire to carry out the policy that the government should own its own buildings, which I think is best all round in the public interest. At no distant date an important move in that direction will perhaps be made, but in view of the difficulty of purchasing land at a moderate price hon. gentlemen should not urge that it should be done too quickly.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: It is a new building with very little additional cost in that case.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: How much has been spent in fitting it up for the use of the government for repairs and furniture and permanent works ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The chief architect tells me in respect to that that there has been nothing on the building itself. There is the furniture and fittings but no alteration to the building.
In any of these cases does the rent of the building include the cost of heating ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: We take an appropriation for heating. In the ease of the Corry building the heat is supplied, but we do not in all cases have the heat furnished. I do not think my hon. friend is correct in saying that for that amount of money we would have twice the accommodation. For instance we have more accommodation in private buildngs than in a building like the Dangevin block. That cost $800,000 and is a very fine building. I am not arguing that the present method is economical or convenient, and I would favour having a very fine and good departmental building erected where these could be concentrated.
What is the total cost of the Corry building ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: We have no knowledge of that.
It occupies a very small portion of land and I am informed the building was constructed very cheaply.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I could not give the information at present.
In the item for buildings Ottawa, including repairs how much of that amount was included for repairs ou rented buildings ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I am told it is not the practice to repair rented buildings. We have to put our own fittings into the buildings but not to repair them.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: A session or two ago a considerable amount was spent on the Sey-bold building.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: It was not for repairs but to be fitted up to suit the department.
Did the minister read a list of the owners of the buildings that have been rented and the price ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
I began to read a list of the buildings but not of the owners. In some places the buildings bear the owner's name, for instance, the Corry building
and the Orme building, which I understand is owned toy Mr. Orme. In most cases the owners are not given. We rent from the Slater estate five rooms for $550, in the Orme building two rooms at $250, from the Great North Western Telegraph Company, five rooms at $500 per annum. These are all the Ottawa buildings.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: That are included in this vote ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: These are the new buildings, the supplementaries that are in consequence of new buildings.

The minister said that it was no use to be in a great hurry to erect buildings in Ottawa. That is a fact, but the cost will not be growing any less next year or in two years. It has always been the case that property owners are glad to sell to the government at a high price and if you have to pay a high price it is as well to pay it this year as next. The buildings now are very much crowded, in the printing office especially you will find in a room fit for four men, six, seven or eight, and in the departmental blocks and the House of Commons every room seems to be much crowded. It is no use trying to be so stingy about it, you may as well go and put up a building if it costs a couple of millions to do it, and then the men who work in the buildings will have some comfort. They are all crowded and many of them cannot work ; they have so many machines there that they cannot hear themselves talking and cannot turn around and it is disagreeable in every way. You might as well do it first as last.
What is the rental of the building on Metcalfe street occupied by the Survey Department ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General

speechtext: Is there a lease ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: It was leased ab'out four years ago for ten years.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext:
It was leased before it was built. It was run up in a hurry at a cost of not more than $15,000. I am satisfied I could build it in our town for less and the government are paying $3,000 a year.
Dominion public buildings-fuel, &c., $13,000.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Does that include Ottawa the same as others ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: No.
Is it bought by tender ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
Yes, the coal is purchased by tender.
Dominion public buildings-salaries, engineers, firemen, caretakers, &e., $19,500.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: The minister will explain this surely.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This applies to buildings throughout the Dominion. The provision in the main estimates was $110,000. This will make our total appropriation $129,000, and we are asking $127,000 for the coming year. The number of the employees necessarily increases as we go on. The number of buildings increased from 195 to 210.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: That would be 15 additional buildings, and it costs $19,000 for the salaries of the engineers, firemen and caretakers, of these fifteen extra buildings. Has there been an overlapping of the account from last year ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This item is made up of the following : New appointments unprovided for last session, $8,584 ; increases in salaries, $2,878 ; temporary cleaners, jobbers, Ac., $7,873 ; total, $19,385.
Who supplies the fuel for the Toronto public buildings ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
The hard coal for last winter was supplied by the Milnes Co., of Toronto. I am not sure who supplied the soft coal.
Ottawa public buildings, including Rideau Hail-removal of snow, $-2,500.
Will the hon. minister please tell us what Rideau Hall cost us this year ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This does not apply to Rideau Hall only, but to the removal of snow from about the public buildings in Ottawa generally.

But we should have it divided so that we should know what Rideau Hall costs. I have a distinct recollection of criticisms that were made by hon. gentlemen opposite of expenditures on Rideau Hall when we were in power.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: But, cannot my hon. friend (Mr. U. Wilson) forget some things ? I cannot give the expenditure for Rideau Hall separately.
But we should be allowed to know what Rideau Hall costs.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: As respects the removal of snow ?
As respects the whole thing.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: That will come up on the next vote.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
I cannot divide the expenditure under this item in relation to the different buildings. But I will promise my hon. friend (Mr. U. Wilson) that, if it is available in the department, I will give him the statement at another time.
Rideau Hall, including grounds-renewals, improvements, furniture and maintenance, additional amount, $8,000.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)

speechtext: Under this item, perhaps the hon. gentleman (Mr. Fielding) can tell us the cost of Rideau Hall ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The appropriation for the current year was $22,000. For next year we are asking $25,000. Then there is this additional appropriation for the current year of $8,000. The appropriation became exhausted in March last and there are works of renewal, repairs and maintenance to about the amount of this estimate.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: That means a total of $30,000 this year ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Yes. The expenditure for 1904 was $17,000, for 1903, $21,700, for 1902, $24,350.
The Auditor General lias here an item showing that Rideau Hall cost $25,050.38 besides $8,000 for fuel and light.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Perhaps the Auditor General groups a number of items together.

The items as given by the Auditor General for Rideau Hall are : Maintenance, $17,017 : repairs and improvements, $5,093.43 ; removal of snow. $1,230.34 :	charged to 1904-5, $1.-
710.51; total, $25,056.38 Besides that, the Earl of Minto was allowed for fuel and light for twelve months $8,000. And the estimate for this year is about $44,000 as I have it.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: No doubt the Auditor General's figures are correct for the grouping of items that he gives. But we confine ourselves to this one item, so that the figures I give are correct in relation to this.
But the minister has not given me the cost of maintaining Rideau Hall for the year ending June 30 next.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I cannot give the hon. gentleman the figures prepared in that way. But I can give it at another stage if he desires it.
Will the hon. gentleman do it ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Yes, I will do it as well as I can.

In the main estimates there is a vote of $22,000. Then there is the removal of snow for Ottawa public buildings, including Rideau Hall, $2,500. Then there is this supplementary vote : Rideau Hall, including grounds, renewals, improvements, furniture and maintenance, additional amount, $8,000.' I think there ought to be some explanation as to why this increased expenditure is necessary.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
As some of these items are not confined to Rideau Hall, but Include ' others, it would be necessary to separate

them, and I will endeavour to do that at a later stage. The Auditor General groups a number of things together, and we will endeavour to do the same.
I would like to have some particular day fixed, because I would like to be here.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
I want to make this suggestion generally, that as respects all these supplementary estimates, I would be glad if hon. gentlemen would, with as little discussion as may be necessary, assist to pass them, because until we can get a Supply Bill there is a little embarrassment. But there will be ample opportunity of discussing every question that hon. gentlemen may wish to discuss. There will be another item in the supplementaries for the coming year in regard to Rideau Hall.
Ottawa departmental buildings-additional fittings for treasury vault, $3,000.
Are these vaults up-to-date and modern ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
I think our vaults generally are up-to-date. We have, so far as I can learn, everything that is possible in the way of security.
Some resolutions reported.

speakeroldname: Hon. W. S. FIELDING (Minister of Finance).
speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: At an earlier stage I called attention to the motion standing in the name of the Prime Minister to the effect that when the House adjourns on Wednesday it shall stand adjourned until Friday, and being informed by some hon. gentlemen that there was a desire not to meet on Friday, I agreed to hold the matter over long enough to afford an opportunity for consultation. I have since been advised that a consultation has taken place, and that on both sides of the House there is a feeling that as Thursday is a holiday, and as Friday is not usually a very busy day, we should not ask the members to come back on Friday, but to adjourn until Monday. On the information that that is agreeable to both sides of the House, I will now amend the Prime Minister's motion to make it read that when the House adjourns on Wednesday, the 31st instant, it stand adjourned until Monday, the 5th of June next.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Motion agreed to.
Mr. FIELDING moved the adjournment of the House.
Mr. TAYLOR, What will be taken up tomorrow, and what will be done with regard to the subject mentioned by the leader of the opposition ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
We will continue the estimate?. After the inquiry to-day I sent a note to the Prime Minister, who replied, 217
and I sent his reply to the leader of the opposition, that he will be in the House tomorrow and will confer with the leader of the opposition about it.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: Motion agreed to, and House adjourned at 11.45 p.m.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: Wednesday, May 31, 1905.
